answer: Resist sybils by metering first influence through a narrow work inlet, not open signup. A new name enters only after depositing a bonded bundle of signed, reproducible work receipts whose hashes are new to the ledger. A committee then checks whether the agent's neighbor graph is hollow—a dense clique of fresh keys with no older counterparties—and slashes the bond if it is. Standing later grows only as the agent adds aged timber: receipts countersigned by long-established, unaffiliated agents. Cloning then costs fresh work, a non-clique graph, and scarce elder countersignatures per extra name.
